title: Tech news today, 23 November 2026

items.headline: Delta flights in and out of Atlanta delayed due to system outage
items.summary: All Delta flights in and out of Atlanta are facing significant delays on Sunday due to a problem with the system that calculates a plane's weight and balance. Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport is Delta's largest hub and one of the busiest airports in the world. While only Delta is impacted at the moment, disruptions at […]
lines: Reported by The Verge: All Delta flights in and out of Atlanta are facing significant delays on Sunday due to a problem with the system that calculates a plane's weight and balance.
Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport is Delta's largest hub and one of the busiest airports in the world, and only Delta is affected at the moment.
For IT teams, the outage shows how a single system failure can delay operations at a major hub.

items.headline: Hackers exploit GL.iNet cloud flaw to infect routers, KVM devices
items.summary: GL.iNet has confirmed that hackers exploited a vulnerability in its cloud remote management services to install custom malware on customers' routers and KVM devices, with some affected users reporting backdoors and reverse shells giving remote access to infected devices. [...]
lines: Reported by BleepingComputer: GL.iNet has confirmed that hackers exploited a vulnerability in its cloud remote management services to install custom malware on customers' routers and KVM devices.
Some affected users reported backdoors and reverse shells that gave remote access to infected devices.
IT teams that manage GL.iNet routers or KVM devices may want to review how those devices are reached through cloud remote management.

items.headline: The Technology Behind More Precise Finding With Galaxy SmartTag3 and SmartThings
items.summary: Samsung Electronics launched Galaxy SmartTag3, a compact tracker that helps locate personal belongings or pets. Weighing just 9.15 g — approximately 33% lighter and 35% smaller by volume than its predecessor — Galaxy SmartTag3 offers improved portability and battery life of up to 550 days under standard usage or 790 days in Power Saving Mode. […]
lines: Samsung Electronics launched Galaxy SmartTag3, a compact tracker that helps locate personal belongings or pets.
The tracker weighs 9.15 g, about 33% lighter and 35% smaller by volume than its predecessor, with battery life of up to 550 days under standard usage or 790 days in Power Saving Mode.
The smaller size and longer battery life offer improved portability and ownership convenience for users who rely on the device to find belongings or pets.

items.headline: RBI releases 2026 list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs)
items.summary: State Bank of India, HDFC Bank, and ICICI Bank continue to be identified as Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs) under the same bucketing structure as in the 2025 list of D-SIBs . The additional Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) requirement for these D-SIBs will be in addition to the capital conservation buffer. The list of D-SIBs is as follows: Bucket Banks Additional Common Equity Tier 1 requirement as a percentage of Risk Weighted Assets (RWAs) 5 - 1% 4 State Bank of India 0.80% 3 - 0.60% 2 HDFC Bank 0.40% 1 ICICI Bank 0.20% Background: The Reserve Bank had issued the Framework for dealing with Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs) on July 22, 2014 , which was subsequently up
lines: The Reserve Bank of India released its 2026 list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs). State Bank of India, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank remain on the list under the same bucketing structure as the 2025 list.

Additional Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) requirements, as a percentage of Risk Weighted Assets, are 0.80% for State Bank of India, 0.40% for HDFC Bank and 0.20% for ICICI Bank, in addition to the capital conservation buffer.
Banking, compliance and finance teams tracking capital requirements should note the updated D-SIB list and its additional CET1 requirements.

source.name: Reserve Bank of India press releases

items.headline: CISA flags critical Cisco RCE flaw as actively exploited in attacks
items.summary: The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warned federal agencies that attackers are now exploiting a recently patched critical Cisco Expressway vulnerability in the wild. [...]
lines: Reported by BleepingComputer: The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warned federal agencies that attackers are exploiting a recently patched critical Cisco Expressway vulnerability in the wild.
The flaw is described as a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in Cisco Expressway.
IT teams running Cisco Expressway should confirm that the patch is applied, since attacks on this flaw are already occurring.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-131914, carries a CVSS score of 9.3 out of 10.0. The issue affects versions 0.9.1.0 and 0.9.1 Beta, and relates to an
lines: Reported by The Hacker News: Researchers urged users to stop using the legacy ASP.NET anti-CSRF library Idunno.AntiCsrf after a critical vulnerability was found being exploited in the wild.
The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-131914, has a CVSS score of 9.3 out of 10.0 and affects versions 0.9.1.0 and 0.9.1 Beta. The headline describes it as allowing unauthenticated remote code execution.
Developers and IT teams using this legacy library should identify affected versions and plan to move off it, as the source advises.

The activity revolves around CVE-2026-84869 (CVSS score: 9.9), a critical ScreenConnect client flaw that allows a guest to transfer and execute a malicious payload on a connecting technician's host. "On November 12, 2026, we observed one managed service
lines: Reported by The Hacker News: Threat actors are exploiting a now-patched ConnectWise ScreenConnect flaw to target managed service provider (MSP) servers.
The flaw, CVE-2026-84869 (CVSS score 9.9), is a critical ScreenConnect client flaw that allows a guest to transfer and execute a malicious payload on a connecting technician's host.

lines: Reported by The Hacker News: N-able disclosed a critical flaw it found while investigating a breach of its Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud email filtering service.
The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-134624, is a server-side request forgery (SSRF) bug that allowed a user with high-level API access to open connections to internal systems of the user's choosing.

items.headline: Apple will focus on affordable models in early 2027 - iPhone 18e, new iPad, new MacBook Neo

We’re already seeing that – the September iPhone event only brought the two iPhone 18 Pro models and Apple’s first foldable. The remaining iPhone models will come next year. It will start with the iPhone 18e in the February-March time frame, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman. This is when Apple is expected to release iOS 27.4. The “.4” releases tend to be a major milestone in the iOS release cycle – any features that...
lines: Reported by GSMArena news: Apple plans to focus on more affordable models in early 2027, including the iPhone 18e, a new iPad and a new MacBook Neo.
According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, the iPhone 18e is expected in the February-March time frame, around when Apple is expected to release iOS 27.4.
Apple CEO John Ternus said he wants the company to move away from a traditional big September announcement and launch new products more often.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-134814 (CVSS score: 9.2 / 8.1), is a case of code injection impacting binary-parser versions prior to 2.3.1. "Binary-parser before 2.3.1 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows
lines: Reported by The Hacker News: A critical security flaw has been disclosed in the binary-parser library that could let an attacker who controls parser definitions execute arbitrary code.
The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-134814, is a code injection issue in binary-parser versions prior to 2.3.1 and is listed with CVSS scores of 9.2 / 8.1.
IT teams that use binary-parser should check whether their installed versions fall below 2.3.1.

items.headline: Google Meet on the web now supports sending 1080p video for all users, enabled by default
items.summary: We’re expanding 1080p Full HD video sending in Google Meet on the web (previously limited to select paid editions) to all users. It is now enabled by default on computers with a 1080p camera and sufficient compute and bandwidth. Meet transmits 1080p only when a participant's video tile is large enough to display it, and automatically scales resolution down when CPU or bandwidth is constrained. Getting started Admins: The default video quality can be configured at the OU or group level in the Admin console, and existing bandwidth-limit settings remain applied. Visit the Help Center to learn more about configuring default video quality . End users: 1080p will be ON by default under Auto on eli
lines: Google Meet on the web now supports 1080p video sending for all users, not only those on select paid editions.

1080p is enabled by default on computers with a 1080p camera and sufficient compute and bandwidth. Meet sends 1080p only when a video tile is large enough to display it and scales down when CPU or bandwidth is constrained.
Admins can set the default video quality at the OU or group level in the Admin console, and existing bandwidth-limit settings remain applied.

items.headline: Make messages in Google Chat from apps and agents easier to read with tables and headings
items.summary: Agents and apps in Google Chat can now send messages formatted with tables and headings. Tables make it easy to compare options, share status trackers, and present data in rows and columns. Headings provide a way to separate long messages, like summaries, reports, and plans, into clear, scannable sections. Developers can add both through the Google Chat API using standard Markdown. Headings support three levels (#, ##, and ###). Text in tables and headings can use formatting like bold, italics, links, and emoji. Everyone in the conversation will see tables and headings when an app or agent sends them. On the web, tables appear in the message, and you can scroll to see wider tables. On Androi
lines: Agents and apps in Google Chat can now send messages formatted with tables and headings through the Google Chat API, using standard Markdown.
Headings support three levels, and tables and headings can include bold, italics, links, and emoji. Everyone in the conversation sees them.
Tables help compare options and present data, while headings separate long summaries, reports, and plans into scannable sections.

items.headline: Cisco Expressway Series Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
items.summary: A vulnerability in the database service feature of Cisco Expressway Series could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker with network access to a Cisco Expressway device to execute arbitrary operating system commands as root . This vulnerability is due to the use of persistent cookies. Additionally, there is insufficient validation of client certificates when the TLS Verify Mode is set to Enabled for clustering, which means that client certificates are not validated. An attacker with possession of the cookies could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to the database service and invoking specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to exe
lines: Cisco disclosed a vulnerability in the database service feature of Cisco Expressway Series that could let an unauthenticated remote attacker with network access run arbitrary OS commands as root.
The flaw stems from persistent cookies and insufficient validation of client certificates when TLS Verify Mode is set to Enabled for clustering.
IT teams running Cisco Expressway devices should check the advisory to determine whether their configurations are affected.

lines: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime instances are now generally available in the AWS GovCloud (US-West) Region.
Runtime instances run agents on Amazon EC2 instances in the customer's account, while AgentCore handles provisioning, patching, scaling, and lifecycle management.

items.headline: Announcing metal size for Amazon EC2 G7 instances
items.summary: Today, AWS announces the general availability of the metal size for Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) G7 instances, accelerated by NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs. G7 instances deliver up to 4.6x AI inference performance and up to 2.1x graphics performance compared to G6. Customers can use the metal size of G7 instances to run physical AI simulations, deploy AI agent sandboxes, and accelerate graphics workloads that need direct access to bare metal infrastructure. G7 metal instances enable customers to run specialized workloads that require a custom virtualization stack, hypervisor-level GPU drivers, or licensing-restricted applications. The metal size of G7 instanc
lines: AWS announced general availability of the metal size for Amazon EC2 G7 instances, accelerated by NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs.
AWS says G7 instances deliver up to 4.6x AI inference performance and up to 2.1x graphics performance compared to G6.
Metal sizes give workloads direct access to bare metal, which suits custom virtualization stacks, hypervisor-level GPU drivers, and licensing-restricted applications.

SageMaker HyperPod is a purpose-built infrastructure for distributed training and fine-tuning of foundation models at scale, designed to reduce infrastructure management overhead. lines: Amazon SageMaker Studio now provides a native visual interface for submitting distributed training jobs, deploying models, and monitoring workloads on SageMaker HyperPod clusters orchestrated with Amazon EKS.
Data scientists can use the visual interface instead of kubectl and Kubernetes manifests for these tasks.
SageMaker HyperPod is infrastructure for distributed training and fine-tuning of foundation models at scale, designed to reduce infrastructure management overhead.

items.summary: The China-aligned threat actor known as Webworm is suspected to be using a custom version of the open-source SoftEther VPN Bridge tool in an attempt to remove recognizable detection fingerprints, while disguising it as network-monitoring software to establish covert remote access to compromised networks. The modified variant "implements various tricks to hide itself from security tools,"
lines: Reported by The Hacker News: the China-aligned threat actor Webworm is suspected of using a custom version of the open-source SoftEther VPN Bridge tool.
